A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MonoCoP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V6 reports original MonoCoP evaluations on KITTI, nuScenes, and Waymo, empirical attribute correlations, and component and architecture ablations.

after.justification: V7 retains original benchmark results, empirical correlations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 changes the selector from choosing the branch with greater predicted reliability to choosing CoP when its reliability exceeds a threshold τ, otherwise choosing the parallel branch. This changes the routing procedure; feature learning, propagation, aggregation, and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same KITTI, frontal nuScenes, and Waymo coverage, including KITTI pedestrians and cyclists in Table A5. No additional dataset, task, or environmental test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark, efficiency, and ablation comparisons. Table 4 changes its emphasis but retains MonoDETR and MonoDGP. New citations do not introduce evaluated baselines; the backbone comparisons remain in Table A2.

E3.justification: The reported training hardware changes from one H100 to one A6000. Ablation metric reporting narrows from IoU 0.7 and 0.5 to 0.7 in Tables 5 and A2–A4, although Table 5's caption still mentions two thresholds. Splits, training budget, and main benchmark protocols remain unchanged; rerunning experiments is not established.

E4.justification: V7 removes the branch-allocation diagnostic comparing GS, random, and oracle routing proportions, and removes lower-IoU evidence from several ablations. The underlying component, ordering, backbone, AttributeNet, and chain-count analyses remain. Table 5f redisplays backbone results already present in v6's Table A2.

E5.justification: Both versions report median KITTI validation performance across five independent runs. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or another statistical reporting procedure. Changes to the uncertainty-based selector concern the method, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes MonoCoP from 37.11M parameters and 59.82 GFLOPs to 42.50M and 71.77 GFLOPs; MonoDETR changes from 59.72 to 62.12 GFLOPs. MonoCoP consequently becomes heavier than MonoDGP in this table. Routing proportions and IoU 0.5 ablation entries are removed, while main benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (11) substantively revises the mathematical definition of branch selection from an argmax over two reliabilities to a threshold rule. The projection derivation, geometric assumptions, and probabilistic depth-loss formulation remain unchanged; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: geometric attribute coupling, complementary CoP and uncertainty-guided selection, and strong detection performance across three benchmarks. The shortened conclusion does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 reframes computational overhead relative to MonoDGP and removes the description of MonoDGP as heavier than MonoCoP. The routing discussion drops its interpretation of allocation proportions as closely matching the oracle. The camera-intrinsics limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V7 newly supplies a repository address and states that code and models are publicly available. It revises the hardware disclosure to A6000 and explicitly attributes the training protocol to MonoDGP. Appendix A's hyperparameters remain unchanged, and the newly introduced routing threshold has no disclosed value or selection procedure.

R1.justification: V7 adds references including MonoDINO-DETR, CHARM3R, MonoCLUE, SeaBird, and multimodal recognition work, extending the overview and future-work discussion. Its central positioning against parallel prediction and output-level autoregressive methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V7 updates affiliations and contact information, corrects some grammar and terminology, shortens the routing discussion and conclusion, and adds a brief backbone paragraph. The overall section organization and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn, and Figure 5 becomes a full-width arrangement using examples already present in Figure A2. Table 5 is reorganized into six panels, while Tables 4 and A2–A4 lose columns or rows and change layout. Appendix qualitative figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V7 adds useful code/model access information and clearer displays, but introduces reproducibility and consistency problems. The new selector requires an unspecified τ and conflicts with the introduction's retained description of comparing both branches. Section 5.3 claims a +2.86 AP gain over MonoDGP, whereas Table 4 implies +1.64. With benchmark evidence unchanged and routing diagnostics removed, these problems produce a limited net decline in the paper's clarity and reliability.
